Euclid's Game with Typed Numbers

Number TheoryGame StrategyDivisibility
Game: Two numbers are on the board. You and the computer take turns writing the difference of two numbers already there, and whoever cannot write a new number loses.
How to play: Type a number and press Enter. Tick Please start if you want the computer to go first.

Look for the math

The difference of any two numbers is divisible by their greatest common divisor. That is the whole game.

What can ever appear

Start with N > M and let g = gcd(N, M). Every difference of two numbers that are multiples of g is again a multiple of g, so only multiples of g up to N can appear. And all of them do, however the game goes: this is Euclid’s algorithm. The test played every possible reply against the computer for every start from 5 to 99 (with up to 16 numbers on the final board) and always ended with exactly the multiples of g up to N on the board.

Who wins

The final board holds N/g numbers, two of them given, so exactly N/g − 2 moves are made, whatever anyone does. The first player wins when that is odd, and the second when it is even. The test checked this for every play from every start. So you can know before you type anything whether to tick Please start: start if N/g − 2 is odd.

The computer

The computer does not play to win; it always writes the smallest new multiple of g that it can, as the applet does. It does not need to be clever: with a won position it only has to wait for you to run out.

The applet checks your number and says Please check your calculations… for a number that is not a multiple of g or is too big, How come? Please try again… for one that is not a difference, and The number is already on the board. The grid version of this game is the page Euclid’s Game.

Start with 12 and 18. What is g, how many numbers will end up on the board, and who wins?

Puzzle by Alexander Bogomolny (cut-the-knot.org)
